about: Quick check for the WCAG 3 audit calculator. Every question maps to one or more core requirements in the WCAG 3 editor's draft. meetsWhen says which answer means the requirement is met. A question with children asks them only after the answer named in when. A question with naWhenNo marks every requirement below it as not applicable when the answer is no. scripts/check-quick-check.mjs verifies every slug exists, is a core requirement, and that every core requirement is either asked about or listed in notTestableYet.

standIns.contrast-text: The draft has not chosen a contrast measure yet. Until it does, WCAG 2.2's 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text is a reasonable stand-in.
standIns.contrast-nontext: The draft has not chosen a contrast measure yet. Until it does, WCAG 2.2's 3:1 for user interface components and graphics is a reasonable stand-in.

notTestableYet.reason: The draft has not set the minimum values for margins, line length and line height yet.
The draft has not set the minimum values for typeface, font size, letter spacing and the other text style properties yet.

items.q: Does every page or screen have a title that describes its name, topic or purpose?
Is the language of the content set in the code, including any passages in a different language?
items.help: For example the lang attribute on the html element, and on any element whose language differs.

items.q: Is all visible text available to assistive technology as text, rather than only as pixels in an image, canvas or vector shapes?
Does all text have enough contrast against its background?
Can text be enlarged to at least 200% of the platform's default body text size?
Can people override text and background colours, for example with a high-contrast mode or browser settings, without losing content or functionality?
Can people override the typeface, font width, text decoration, capitalization and hyphenation of text without losing content or functionality?
items.help: For example with a user stylesheet or a reading extension.

items.q: Can people adjust margins, line length, line height and justification of paragraphs without losing content or functionality?
Are abbreviations explained or expanded the first time they are used?
items.help: Words like HTML or scuba that have their own dictionary entry don't need it.

items.q: Are dates, times, temperatures and Roman numerals written so they can't be misread, and marked up with a machine-readable equivalent?
items.help: For example 3 May 2025 rather than 03/05/2025, and a time element with a datetime value.

items.q: Is bold, italic, size or other styling ever used to carry meaning beyond emphasis, such as marking an error?

children.q: Is that meaning also available to assistive technology, for example as text or an icon with a name?

items.q: Do you have pages with long-form text, 300 words or more organized in paragraphs?

children.q: Does each of those pages have a summary that is marked as one, uses short sentences, and explains any uncommon words?
children.help: When long text continues across several pages, only the first one needs a summary.

items.q: Is any content in a language that is often written without diacritics for proficient readers, such as Hebrew or Arabic?

children.q: Are the diacritics needed to identify the correct meaning of each word available?

items.q: Are distinct blocks of content, such as navigation, main content, sidebars and cards, marked up as such in the code and separated by enough space on screen?
Do those blocks have a heading or label that says what they're for, where the purpose isn't already obvious?
Are ordered items, such as numbered lists and the steps of a process, marked up so their position can be read out?
Does the content work in the device's default orientation, or in both portrait and landscape on devices that have no default?
Does any content appear on top of the main content, such as cookie banners, pop-ups, chat widgets or dialogs?

children.q: Can every one of them be dismissed?

items.q: Do you have multi-step processes, such as a checkout, sign-up or wizard?

children.q: Is a list of all the steps shown and available to assistive technology at each step?
children.help: Not needed when the number of steps is unknown or depends on what the user does.

children.q: Is the current step shown visually and in the code?
Can people finish without having to remember information from an earlier step?

items.q: Is any information shown by colour alone, such as red meaning an error or a line on a chart told apart only by colour?
Do any instructions rely only on shape, colour, size, position or sound, such as press the round button on the right?
Is any information given by sound alone, such as a chime that is the only sign of a new message?
items.help: Audio-based media, such as a podcast, is exempt.

gate.q: Does your site use images, icons, charts or other graphics?

items.q: Does every image that isn't purely decorative have a text alternative?
Does each text alternative convey the same purpose as its image?
Are purely decorative images hidden from assistive technology?
Can assistive technology tell that informative images are images?
items.help: For example an img element, or role=img on a custom graphic.

items.q: Does all other non-decorative non-text content, such as charts, canvas drawings and SVG icons, have an equivalent text alternative in the code?
Do the parts of graphics needed to understand them have enough contrast?
Is any information conveyed only through visual depth, such as a 3D effect?

gate.q: Does your site have prerecorded audio or video?

items.q: Does any of it include speech or other sound that matters for understanding it?
items.help: Background music with no spoken content doesn't count.

children.q: Are captions available for all of it?
children.help: Media that is an alternative for text on the page, and clearly labelled as such, is exempt.

children.q: Are the captions complete and accurate, so they are equivalent to the audio?
Are the captions in sync with the audio?
Do the captions identify or describe sounds needed to understand the media, and explain nonverbal cues such as tone?
Is a dialogue transcript available for all of it?
Is the transcript placed next to the audio or video it belongs to?
Are transcripts complete and accurate, including sounds and nonverbal cues needed to understand the media?

items.q: Does any video show information that isn't in its audio, such as on-screen text, charts, actions or scene changes?

children.q: Are audio descriptions available that describe that visual information?
Do the audio descriptions convey everything the visuals do, including nonverbal cues, and sounds where needed?
Do the audio descriptions fit in the gaps without talking over dialogue or other meaningful sound?
Are the natural pauses in the soundtrack ever too short to fit the descriptions?
Does the video pause to make room for extended audio descriptions that cover the visual information completely?
Is a descriptive transcript available that includes the visual information as well as the dialogue?

gate.q: Does your site stream live audio or video, or offer voice calls?

items.q: Do you stream live audio or video with speech?

children.q: Are captions available for all live audio?
Are dialogue transcripts available for all live audio and video?

items.q: Do you offer real-time two-way voice communication, such as calls or voice chat?

children.q: Is a real-time text option available?

gate.q: Does any audio play automatically, including notification sounds?

items.q: Can people pause it, stop it and set its volume separately from the system volume?
items.help: A single site-wide control that turns sounds off can meet this.

gate.q: Does your site have animation, video, carousels or other moving or flashing content?

items.q: Does any motion or pseudo-motion last longer than 5 seconds, apart from motion that is essential?
items.help: Pseudo-motion is something that looks like it moves without moving, such as some patterns.

items.q: Does anything flash above the general flash or red flash thresholds, apart from flashing that is essential?
items.help: If people can set an accessibility-supported preference that stops flashing and you respect it, answer no.

items.q: Does any single change from light to dark, or dark to light, cover more than 30% of the screen with a contrast change over 4.5:1, other than a new page loading?
Is there still any flashing, pseudo-motion, or motion over 5 seconds, for example because it is essential?

children.q: Is there a warning before people encounter it, and a way to get the same information without it?

items.q: Can every control be operated with a keyboard alone?
Can all content be reached with a keyboard alone, including content shown on hover or right-click and content far down a page?
Can the keyboard always move both forward to the next interactive element and back to the previous one?
Can people always leave a component they entered with the keyboard, such as a dialog, menu, date picker or video player, using standard keys?
items.help: Non-standard keys are fine if they are explained on the page or earlier in the process.

items.q: Does keyboard focus move in an order that preserves meaning and lets people operate things?
Does focus skip hidden content and non-interactive content, and avoid stopping on long groups of repeated controls?
Does focus move only when the user does something?
items.help: Exceptions include moving to the next field of a one-time code, safety warnings such as an imminent timeout, and moves the user is told about first and can avoid.

items.q: When focus changes automatically or when something receives focus, is the change shown on screen and announced?
After someone clicks or taps on the page, does the next press of Tab start from where they clicked?
Have you replaced the browser's default focus indicator with your own?

children.q: Does your focus indicator have enough contrast against what is next to it, and a clear change of contrast from the unfocused state?

items.q: Do you have custom keyboard shortcuts?

children.q: Do they avoid conflicting with standard platform shortcuts, or can people remap them?

items.q: Does any content appear when people hover over or focus on something, such as tooltips or fly-out menus?
items.help: Browser tooltips from the title attribute don't count; this is about content you control.

children.q: Can people move the pointer onto that content without it disappearing?
If it covers other content, can people dismiss it without moving the pointer or focus, for example with Escape?

items.q: Does every interactive element have a persistent visible label or icon, and an accessible name in the code that says what it does?
items.help: Placeholder text that disappears when people type isn't persistent.

items.q: Does each accessible name include the visible label text?
Do custom controls expose an accurate name, role, value and state, such as expanded, selected or checked?
When a control's name, role, value or state changes, is the change shown on screen and exposed in the code?
Do the visual parts that identify controls and their states, such as borders and checkmarks, have enough contrast?
items.help: Controls left in the browser's default style, and inactive controls, are exempt.

items.q: Can everything done by dragging, double-clicking, swiping or multi-finger gestures also be done with single clicks or taps that don't need timing?
Is any function only possible with a path-based gesture, such as drawing a shape or swiping along a route, where that isn't essential?
Do clicks and taps take effect when released rather than when pressed, or can people cancel or undo them?
Does anything require a particular pointer pressure or speed, where that isn't essential?

gate.q: Does your site have forms or other places where people enter data?

items.q: Are input requirements, such as required fields, date formats and password rules, shown before people enter data?
When an error is detected, is it identified and described in text?
Is each validation error linked, visually and in the code, to the field that caused it or can fix it?
Before submitting, can people review and correct what they entered, or the errors found?
items.help: Not needed when entries are saved automatically or can be reversed.

items.q: Can people paste, and use browser autofill or password managers, in every field for personal information?

gate.q: Do people sign in or verify who they are?

items.q: Can people complete sign-in without a cognitive function test, such as solving a puzzle or remembering and typing a password unaided?
items.help: Allowing password managers and paste, passkeys or email links are common ways to offer this.

items.q: Do you use biometrics, such as a face, fingerprint or voice?

children.q: Is there always a way to sign in that isn't biometric?

gate.q: Do people make choices with legal, financial, privacy or security consequences, such as purchases, consent or sharing data?

items.q: Is each of those choices accompanied by a description of its benefits, risks and potential consequences?
Are preselected options that affect money, privacy or safety, such as opt-ins, visible and exposed in the code by default?
Does the site show or ask for personal or sensitive information?

children.q: Are people who use assistive technology, accessible versions or accessibility settings exposed to no extra risk, such as a password being read aloud?

items.q: Are meaningful changes on screen, such as status messages, new content above the current position, or a changed number of results, conveyed to assistive technology?
When content changes to a new page or view without a full page load, is there a visible change and a programmatic notification?
Does content ever open a new window, switch apps or change device settings automatically?

children.q: Are people told before it happens?

items.q: Does the content respond to people's platform and browser accessibility settings, such as font size, colour scheme, magnification and reduced motion?
Can the content be controlled with assistive and adaptive technology, such as screen readers, voice control and switch access?
Can screen reader users reach all content and interactions in browse mode or with a virtual cursor, not only with Tab?

gate.q: Does your product use vibration, body movement, eye tracking, speech input, a custom or hidden pointer, touch-only or VR input, or 360-degree environments?

items.q: Does it trigger vibration or other haptic feedback?

children.q: Can people reduce or turn off the haptic feedback?

items.q: Does any feature use body movement such as shaking, eye tracking, or speaking?

children.q: Is there always another way to use each of those features, unless that input is essential?

items.q: Do you change, hide or replace the pointer, or run on a platform without a visible pointer, such as touch or VR?

children.q: Is a visible pointer indicator always shown where the platform has one?
children.help: It may hide over a video when it isn't moving, or when the pointer steers the view in a virtual environment.

children.q: If you change the pointer's look, is the default pointer at least as large as the platform's and does it have enough contrast?
Where there is no visible pointer, such as touch or VR, is there a visible sign that something has been selected?

items.q: Do you have 360-degree, virtual or augmented reality content?

children.q: Where people control where captions appear, do captions stay directly in front of them?
When sound or speech comes from outside the current view, is its direction indicated?
Is any information conveyed only by where a sound seems to come from?
If audio shifts to create a sense of motion, can people pause or turn that off?
children.help: Answer yes if the content never shifts audio this way.
